20.3 Depression
Depression affects the capabilities of the driver:
Increasing distractions. The driver focuses all his attention on his thoughts and neglects the surroundings.
Making valuable information become lost or irrelevant. The driver fails to detect significant information needed for safety and requiring driver reaction, especially in more complex situations.
Increasing insecurity. Depression interferes in the decision-making process, so the driver can make mistakes or act unpredictably.
Increasing the propensity for sleepiness and fatigue. It is advisable not to drive at night or in environments where road monotony may occur or for long periods of time.
Increasing irritability and anxiety. A trivial event can provoke a disproportionate reaction by the driver.
In addition, there is usually the need for psychotropic drugs, which can directly affect the ability to drive.

This plate is placed at the rear of a vehicle to indicate that the vehicle or set of vehicles is longer than 12 metres in length. It is a yellow, reflective rectangular plate framed by a fluorescent red border.
Alternatively, smaller plates may be used and more conveniently located symmetrically on the vehicle.
(Página 220 del manual 'Learning to drive')

7 Headlights – main beam / high beam / long range
 
7.2 Use of main beam / high beam / long range headlights
Except when using dipped (low beam) headlight, all vehicles (required to have main beam headlights fitted) must use them when travelling, outside a built-uparea and at more than 40 km/h:
Between the hours of sunset and sunrise when driving on an insufficiently illuminated road.
(Página 100 del manual 'Learning to drive')

7 Headlights – main beam / high beam / long range  
 
7.2 Use of main beam / high beam / long range headlights
Except when using dipped (low beam) headlight, all vehicles (required to have main beam headlights fitted) must use them when travelling, outside a built-uparea and at more than 40 km/h:
During any time of the day, when driving in tunnels, underpasses and sections of road where the “unnel” sign is displayed and there is insufficient lighting.
It is optional to use main beam headlights, outside a built-up-area, when travelling at or below 40 km/h.  
Remember: Main beam headlights may cause dazzle and discomfort to other road users and must be substituted to dipped, low beam lights when the situation requires this.
(Página 100 del manual 'Learning to drive')

10 Immobilisations – Stationary vehicles Stopping (waiting) and parking  
10.4 Parking and stopping / waiting – unacceptable practises
In this respect, stopping (waiting) and parking in the following places are considered particularly dangerous or would be such as to prevent the circulation of others and constitute an obvious hazard and obstruction to others:
When the distance between the vehicle and the opposite edge of the roadway (or a solid line) is less than 3 metres or the gap is such that it does not allow other vehicles to pass.
When the vehicle is stopped or parked in such a manner as to prevent other vehicles entering onto the road and into the circulation of the traffic.
When the vehicle is stopped or parked so as to prevent normal and regular access and passage to people or animal entering or exiting a building.
(Página 199 del manual 'Learning to drive')

DRIVING ASSIST SYSTEMS  
   
15 Lane Keep Assist (LKA)
The system controls the direction of the vehicle to keep it inside the lane, preventing it from drifting outside the lane if the driver is distracted or drowsy. Together with the LDW system, it monitors the vehicle’s position with respect to the lines delimiting the lane along which it is travelling. If the vehicle leaves, or is about to leave, the lane and the indicators have not been activated, it gently steers the vehicle back to the correct position.
(Página 93 del manual 'Learning to drive')
